normalisations: Request IDs are fixed: the 12 bytes of "vector-id-v1", then the exchange's number, big-endian, in the last 4 bytes. Database names are fixed (v001, v002, ...), one per exchange.

Values that differ from run to run (each listed in its vector's response.vary, a path with [] for every array element) are replaced inside the BSON by a fixed value of the same BSON type: a string by "normalised", an int32 or int64 by 1, a double by 1.0, a datetime by 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z, a binary by the bytes of "normalised" with its subtype kept, an array by an empty array and a document by an empty document; the payload is then re-encoded. A driver checks a varying field's presence and BSON type, not its value.

Document field order: the server holds a stored document, and every document a request type declares as a map, as a Go map and encodes it in an unspecified order that differs from run to run. So the fields of every nested document in a request, and of every stored document in an answer (under data, doc, documents, results, value, element, metadata and values, and the document after a GET_FAST answer's status byte), are sorted by name. A driver compares documents field by field, never by their bytes.

Loopback ports the run happened to get are rewritten to fixed ones inside every string outside a stored document (the single node's driver port to 7433 and ring port to 4433; node1, node2 and node3 of the three-node cluster to driver ports 7433, 7434, 7435 and ring ports 4433, 4435, 4437; the not-yet-added node to 7436 and 4439), and the run's temporary directory to /data.
Server identities are fixed ed25519 keys made from fixed seeds, so fingerprints are the same in every run and are not normalised.

Fields that describe the capturing host rather than the protocol (health's capacity, wal and memtable) are removed from the captured answer and listed in additive_fields: a driver must accept them and may not require them.

An ERROR answer written by the transport layer (its only fields are code and message) is encoded from a Go map, so its two fields arrive in either order; they are recorded sorted (code, then message).

The bucket is at three copies, its owner is node2 and node3 is the copy a decrease to two keeps; node3 cannot show it holds what node1's copy holds, so the owner refuses the decrease. The request goes to node1, which forwards it: the refusal is an ERROR frame UNAVAILABLE with write_outcome not_applied whichever node answers, because nothing changed and a retry is safe once node3 is back and has caught up. The refusals of an owner that clear by retrying (a placement pass still running, a copy still being made, a member that runs an older version) carry the same code and outcome.

Run 'show buckets' on node2 and retry when the row reads 3/3. If node3 is not coming back, run 'remove-node node3' first.

vectors.name: ring keyed: get one document
vectors.notes: RING_KEYED is binary: a 20-byte client prologue (epoch, state_seq, deadline), the class byte 0x81 get, the 40-byte header and the encoded document id. The reply is a RING_REPLY with found and the document's BSON in elements.

vectors.name: ring keyed: insert one document
vectors.notes: A write class (0x01 insert) carries the document id value and the fields by field id. The reply carries write_outcome, copies_confirmed, served_by, position and the id the insert used.

vectors.name: ring keyed: read one element by key (store_get)
vectors.notes: Read class 0x88 store_get reads one element of a hashStore or btreeStore by its key, or of a heapStore by its entry id: the class byte, the 40-byte header, the document id, the 2-byte field id, then a 2-byte key length and the key (1 to 1024 bytes). The reply is found and the element in elements; a key that is not there is found false. It takes no position.

vectors.name: ring keyed: a hashStore page carries the keys
vectors.notes: A store list of a hashStore or btreeStore replies with keys, one string per element in the same order as elements; a heapStore's list also carries priorities, and a fifoStore's or lifoStore's carries neither. Absent members are omitted.

vectors.name: ring keyed: a heapStore peek carries entry ids and priorities
vectors.notes: A peek of a heapStore replies with keys (the entry ids) and priorities (int64), parallel to elements, highest priority first. A peek count is 1 to 100.

vectors.name: ring keyed refused: a peek of more than 100
vectors.notes: The peek count is 1 to 100, the same cap the server enforces for a pop.

vectors.name: ring keyed: pop up to three elements
vectors.notes: A pop with no arg takes one element. A pop with the arg {n: int32} (a BSON document, n 1 to 100) takes up to n in one record and replies with them in elements, found true when at least one came out. All the elements must fit the 1024 bytes of a dedupe entry together, or the pop is refused RESULT_TOO_LARGE before it is applied, naming the count that fits.

vectors.name: ring batch: three writes, one refused
vectors.notes: RING_BATCH is binary: the 20-byte client prologue once, a count byte (1 to 255), then that many RING_KEYED write bodies back to back (class byte, 40-byte header, class form). Reads are not allowed. The reply is a RING_REPLY with outcome (ok when every operation was answered with a reply, partial when any was refused) and answers, one per operation in request order: each is {reply: the bytes of a lone RING_REPLY} or {error: the bytes of an OpError payload}. A refused operation does not stop the others, and there is no atomicity across them. To retry, send the whole frame again under the same request id: the operations that were applied answer deduped.

vectors.name: ring batch: every operation applied
vectors.notes: One operation, answered as the lone RING_KEYED would be: outcome ok and one answer.

vectors.name: ring batch refused: a count of zero
vectors.notes: A batch carries 1 to 255 operations.

vectors.name: ring batch refused: a trailing byte
vectors.notes: Nothing follows the last operation.

vectors.name: ring batch refused: truncated
vectors.notes: The last operation is cut short.

vectors.name: ring batch refused: a read class
vectors.notes: A batch carries writes only; the error names the operation.

vectors.name: ring batch: a frame that does not decode is refused whole
vectors.notes: A payload that is not a prologue and a count is one OpError, INVALID_ARGUMENT; nothing was done. A refusal of one operation is an answer inside a RING_REPLY instead.

vectors.name: ring batch refused: a count past the operations

vectors.name: ring batch: a batch of one answers as the lone request would
vectors.notes: A batch of one is operation 0 under the request id, so its inner reply is byte-equal to the reply of the lone RING_KEYED insert vector, and its dedupe entry is that request's.

vectors.name: ring batch: 255 operations, the most a frame holds
vectors.notes: The count byte is 255: the largest frame, answered with 255 answers in request order. A 256th operation cannot be written (the count is one byte and the index of an operation is one byte of its dedupe key), so a driver refuses it when it queues it, before sending anything: 'at most 255 ... Split it into batches of 255 or fewer'.

vectors.name: ring batch: a reply over the budget drops a claim's elements, not the claim
vectors.notes: The reply budget is min(max_result_bytes, 16 MiB). A recomputable reply that does not fit keeps write_outcome, copies_confirmed, position, deduped, found, id, served_by and the lease and drops elements, keys and priorities: the claim stays applied, its lease id stays, and lease_get reads the leased messages back. A pop or take answer is never trimmed; one the budget has no room for is not run and is answered UNAVAILABLE, not attempted.

vectors.name: ring batch: the deadline leaves a not-attempted tail
vectors.notes: deadline_ms is the whole frame's budget. Once it is spent the operations not yet started are answered UNAVAILABLE saying not attempted, not applied, and to resend the whole frame with the same request id; they are never unknown. Which operations fall in the tail is not deterministic when more than one pair is in flight. The caller sends the whole frame again under the same request id: the applied operation answers deduped, the others run.

vectors.name: ring batch reply refused: ok over a refused answer
vectors.notes: outcome is partial when any answer is an error.

vectors.name: ring topology: the first call after AUTH

When every term holds the reply is the ordinary applied reply plus document, a BSON document of the scalar fields, _id_ first, as the update left it (return after) or as it was (return before).

vectors.name: ring update guard refused
vectors.notes: A guard that does not hold is a successful RING_REPLY, not an OpError: write_outcome not_applied, reason guard, guard_field naming the first field that differed and document, the current document. It has no position and no copies_confirmed, because nothing was written and no position was taken. A retry under the same request id is evaluated again.

vectors.name: ring keyed: get of an expired document
vectors.notes: NOT_FOUND carries the detail {expired: true} when the document exists but its expire time has passed: the owner treats it as absent until the sweep removes it. A plain miss has no detail. A driver acts on detail.expired, never on the text, and still treats both as not found.

payload_json.message: document "ada" is not in app.User. The document expired: its 'expire at' time has passed, so it reads as absent until the sweep removes it

vectors.name: ring list: expand an author field
vectors.notes: expand names the scalar fields whose values are ids of another bucket; the node reads each distinct id once by key and answers with expanded, one document per row in row order, each member {expanded: true, doc} or {expanded: false, reason}. A document that is gone is expanded false, never an error. served_from says whether a copy on the node answered (local) or the owner (owner).

vectors.name: ring keyed: a get_fields with expand and local
vectors.notes: Read classes 0x81, 0x83 and 0x89 take an optional trailer after their class form: a 2-byte length and a BSON document {local, expand: [{field, database, bucket, fields, where}]}, at most 8 expansions. No other class takes it.

vectors.name: ring keyed: a get with local (0x81 trailer)
vectors.notes: Read class 0x81 get takes the same optional trailer as 0x83 and 0x89: the class form, then a 2-byte length and a BSON document. local asks a ready copy on the node to answer; served_from says which side did.

vectors.name: ring keyed: a hashStore page with expand (0x83 trailer)
vectors.notes: Read class 0x83 store list takes the trailer too: expand names the bucket whose documents the element keys are the ids of (a spec with no field, since the store is the field). The reply carries expanded, one member per element in order.

vectors.name: ring keyed refused: an empty options trailer
vectors.notes: A trailer that names neither local nor expand has no encoding: an empty options set is no trailer at all.

vectors.name: ring admin: create a bucket with aggregates
vectors.notes: aggregates is a list of {store, kind, field, by} after fields: kind is sum, sum by or count by, field is the summed element path (absent for count by) and by the grouping path (absent for sum). The reply's aggregates list each one with its id and state.

vectors.name: ring store: sum
vectors.notes: Read class 0x8B names the store field, then kind 1 (sum), the summed path and no by. One number: an int64 until a double was added to the store, a double after; 0 for an empty store.

vectors.name: ring store: sum by
vectors.notes: Kind 2 names both paths. The reply's values are in by order, each {by, sum, n}; more and cursor page a long list, the cursor being the last by key.

vectors.name: ring store: count by
vectors.notes: Kind 3 names the by path only; each value is {by, n}.

vectors.name: ring store: describe aggregates
vectors.notes: Kind 0 names nothing and lists every aggregate the store keeps with its state and value (a by form: how many distinct values it holds, and a warning above 10000).

vectors.name: ring store: aggregate not declared
vectors.notes: A read of an aggregate the store does not keep is INVALID_ARGUMENT with AGGREGATE_NOT_DECLARED first, the aggregates it does keep, and the statement that declares one.

payload_json.message: AGGREGATE_NOT_DECLARED: app.Property.Expenses keeps no "sum Amout" (it keeps: [sum Amount]). Nothing was read. An aggregate is declared when the bucket is created, as in 'create bucket Property in app { Expenses btreeStore with (sum Amount, sum Amount by Currency, count by Category) }'

vectors.name: ring store: inc creates an element
vectors.notes: Verb 5 on a hashStore or btreeStore adds to the numbers of the element under k, and creates the element when k is absent. The arg is {k: string, v: a BSON document of dotted paths (three levels at most) to int32, int64 or finite double amounts, r omitted}; an amount that is not a number, a decimal included, is INVALID_ARGUMENT. The reply is the ordinary write acknowledgement.

vectors.name: ring store: inc with return after
vectors.notes: The arg adds r: true (written only when true, so an arg has one byte form). The element as applied comes back in elements with found true; a retry with the same request id is answered the same element and nothing is added twice.

vectors.name: ring get-many: every key found, in request order
vectors.notes: RING_GET_MANY is binary: the 20-byte client prologue once, a count byte (1 to 255), then each key as a 2-byte big-endian length and the body of a RING_KEYED get (0x81) or get_fields (0x89) read. The reply is a RING_REPLY with outcome (ok when every key was answered with a reply, partial when any was answered with an error) and answers, one per key in request order: each is {reply: the bytes of a lone get reply} or {error: the bytes of an OpError payload}. Reads only; keys may differ in bucket; no atomicity, no snapshot.

vectors.name: ring get-many: two buckets, a miss and a get_fields
vectors.notes: Each body carries its own 40-byte header, so one frame names keys of different buckets (and databases). A document that is gone is found:false, an answer and not an error; the drivers' rule that a miss is a typed not-found error applies to a single-value read only. get_fields returns only the named scalars. A repeated key is answered twice and read once. Reads only; keys may differ in bucket; no atomicity, no snapshot.

vectors.name: ring get-many: a key answered from a ready copy says so
vectors.notes: local: true on a key (the options trailer of its body) lets a ready copy on the receiving node answer it; the answer then carries served_from local. Keys that are not local are read at their owner. Reads only; keys may differ in bucket; no atomicity, no snapshot.

vectors.name: ring get-many: one key refused, the others answered
vectors.notes: Authorization is per key: a key on a bucket the session may not read answers the uniform PERMISSION_DENIED (it names neither the bucket nor whether it exists) and the outcome is partial. A refused key does not stop the others. Reads only; keys may differ in bucket; no atomicity, no snapshot.

vectors.name: ring get-many: a key over the reply budget
vectors.notes: The reply holds at most min(max_result_bytes, 16 MiB), charged as each found document arrives; found:false and error answers are always kept. A document that does not fit what is left answers RESULT_TOO_LARGE naming the key; a key not read because the reply was already full answers RESULT_TOO_LARGE too ('the 16 MiB reply was already full, so it was not read'); a document larger than the whole budget says 'Read this document with Get'. Ask again for such keys in a smaller frame. Reads only; keys may differ in bucket; no atomicity, no snapshot.

vectors.name: ring get-many: the deadline leaves a key not read
vectors.notes: deadline_ms is the frame's budget. A key not read when it is spent answers UNAVAILABLE ('was not read'); one cut off while it was being read answers UNAVAILABLE ('was cut off while it was being read'). Reads change nothing, so resending is safe. Which keys fall in the tail is not deterministic. Reads only; keys may differ in bucket; no atomicity, no snapshot.

vectors.name: ring get-many: a key length past the bytes left is refused whole
vectors.notes: Each key is its 2-byte length and exactly that many bytes of body; the decoder never guesses where a body ends. A frame that does not decode is one OpError, INVALID_ARGUMENT, naming the key where decoding stopped; nothing was read. Reads only; keys may differ in bucket; no atomicity, no snapshot.

payload_json.message: key 1 of 3 claims 4096 bytes and 97 remain. Nothing was read; send each key as the 2-byte byte length of its read body and then exactly that many bytes

vectors.name: ring get-many: a key length of zero is refused whole
vectors.notes: A body is at least its class byte, so a length of 0 is never a key. A frame that does not decode is one OpError, INVALID_ARGUMENT, naming the key where decoding stopped; nothing was read. Reads only; keys may differ in bucket; no atomicity, no snapshot.

payload_json.message: key 1 of 3 has a length of 0. Nothing was read; send each key as the 2-byte byte length of its read body and then the body

vectors.name: ring get-many: a count of zero is refused whole
vectors.notes: A frame carries 1 to 255 keys. A frame that does not decode is one OpError, INVALID_ARGUMENT, naming the key where decoding stopped; nothing was read. Reads only; keys may differ in bucket; no atomicity, no snapshot.

payload_json.message: RING_GET_MANY carries 0 keys. Send 1 to 255 keys, or use Get for one

vectors.name: ring get-many: a write class names its key
vectors.notes: Only get and get_fields are admitted; the refusal names the class and says to send writes in a RING_BATCH. A frame that does not decode is one OpError, INVALID_ARGUMENT, naming the key where decoding stopped; nothing was read. Reads only; keys may differ in bucket; no atomicity, no snapshot.

payload_json.message: key 2 of 3 is an update (class 0x02). A get-many reads documents only; send writes in a RING_BATCH (Bucket.In(batch))

vectors.name: ring get-many: a store read names its key
vectors.notes: A get-many reads whole documents; any other read class is refused naming the class. A frame that does not decode is one OpError, INVALID_ARGUMENT, naming the key where decoding stopped; nothing was read. Reads only; keys may differ in bucket; no atomicity, no snapshot.

payload_json.message: key 1 of 3 is a store list (class 0x83). A get-many reads whole documents (get 0x81, get_fields 0x89); read a store with StoreList

vectors.name: ring get-many refused: a count past the keys
vectors.notes: The count says 4 and 3 keys follow.

vectors.name: ring get-many refused: a trailing byte
vectors.notes: Nothing follows the last key.

vectors.name: ring get-many refused: truncated
vectors.notes: The last key is cut short.

vectors.name: ring get-many refused: a key whose length ends inside its own body
vectors.notes: A length shorter than the body cuts the key short; the cut slice is decoded as a whole body and refused.

vectors.name: ring get-many refused: expand on a key
vectors.notes: A get-many does not expand; use GetExpanded for one document.

vectors.name: ring keyed: upsert
vectors.notes: Write class 0x03 upsert has insert's form: the document id value, then the fields by field id. It stores the document whether or not one exists, so it is never DOCUMENT_EXISTS. The reply is insert's: write_outcome, copies_confirmed, served_by, position and the id.

vectors.name: ring keyed: delete
vectors.notes: Write class 0x04 delete carries no fields: the class byte, the 40-byte header, the document id and one trailer byte, 0x00 when the delete has no guard and asks for no document back. The reply is the write acknowledgement, with no id. A document that is not there is NOT_FOUND.

vectors.name: ring store: push
vectors.notes: Write class 0x05 store verb is the class byte, the 40-byte header, the document id, the 2-byte field id, the verb byte, a 4-byte arg length and the arg, a BSON document. Verb 1 push to a fifoStore or lifoStore takes {v: the element}; a heapStore's push takes {p: int64 priority, e: entry id, v: the element}. The reply is the write acknowledgement.

vectors.name: ring store: put
vectors.notes: Verb 4 put on a hashStore or btreeStore takes {k: the element key, v: the element} and replaces an element that has the key. The reply is the write acknowledgement.

vectors.name: ring store: take
vectors.notes: Verb 3 take on a hashStore or btreeStore takes {k: the element key} (a heapStore's takes {e: the entry id}) and removes that element. The reply is the write acknowledgement plus found and the removed element in elements; a key that is not there is found false with no elements.

vectors.name: ring store: store count
vectors.notes: Read class 0x84 store count is the class byte, the 40-byte header, the document id and the 2-byte field id, with nothing after it. The reply is count as int64, the number of elements in that store field of that document; a present zero is written. It takes no position.

vectors.name: ring lease: claim
vectors.notes: Write class 0x06 claim leases messages of a fifoStore or lifoStore without removing them: the class byte, the 40-byte header, the document id, the 2-byte field id, a 2-byte count (1 to 65535), then an 8-byte clock and a 16-byte nonce that the owner stamps and a client sends as zeros. The reply is the write acknowledgement plus the leased messages in elements and lease, the 16-byte lease id. A field with nothing to lease answers no elements and no lease.

vectors.name: ring lease: ack
vectors.notes: Write class 0x07 ack removes a lease's messages for good: the class byte, the 40-byte header, the document id, the 2-byte field id, the 16-byte lease id a claim returned, then the 8-byte clock the owner stamps (zeros from a client). The reply is the write acknowledgement alone; it carries no found.

vectors.name: ring lease: release
vectors.notes: Write class 0x08 release has ack's form and puts a lease's messages back in the field. The reply is the write acknowledgement plus found: true when the lease was live, false for a lease that is unknown or past its deadline, which is an answer and not an error.

vectors.name: ring lease: extend
vectors.notes: Write class 0x09 extend has ack's form plus 8 bytes: how long the lease lasts from now, in milliseconds (1000 to 3600000); the owner turns it into the deadline. The reply is release's: the write acknowledgement plus found, true when the lease was live.

vectors.name: ring lease: lease_get
vectors.notes: Read class 0x87 lease_get reads the messages a lease still holds, so a client that lost a claim's reply recovers them: the class byte, the 40-byte header, the document id, the 2-byte field id and the 16-byte lease id. The reply is found, the leased messages in elements, in claim order, and the lease id again; a lease that is unknown, acked, released or past its deadline is found false with no elements. It takes no position.

vectors.name: ring store: nearest
vectors.notes: Read class 0x8A nearest returns the k elements of one store field closest to a query vector: the class byte, the 40-byte header, the document id, the 2-byte field id, a metric byte (0x01 cosine, 0x02 dot, 0x03 l2), k (1 to 100), a 1-byte name length and the name of the element key that holds the vector, then a 2-byte vector length and the vector, little-endian float32 values (4 to 16384 bytes). The reply is found, the elements best first, their keys (a hashStore or btreeStore) or entry ids (a heapStore), scores, one double per element, and scanned and skipped as int32: the elements scored and the elements without the vector key. It takes no position.

vectors.name: ring update: every operator code
vectors.notes: An update's field entry is the operator code, the 2-byte field id, a 4-byte value length and the value, one entry per field id in request order. The codes are 0x01 set (a typed value), 0x02 unset (the value is BSON null), 0x03 inc, 0x04 mul, 0x05 push and 0x06 add to set (an array), 0x07 min and 0x08 max, and 0x09 rename, whose value is the 2-byte target field id and no type byte. The reply is the ordinary write acknowledgement.

vectors.name: ring update: a guard of sixteen terms, return before
vectors.notes: A guard holds 1 to 16 equalities on fields 2 and up in ascending order, each a 2-byte field id, a 4-byte value length and the typed value. Bits 1 and 2 of the trailer hold the return mode: 1 after, 2 before. return before answers the document as it was before the update, _id_ first; the guard rides the client body only and a record body carries the return alone.

vectors.name: ring keyed: an insert of every declared width
vectors.notes: A field value is its BSON type byte then the value's bytes, and the server stores the width it is sent: int32 for a word that fits, int64 for a whole value past int32 (3e9 here), double, decimal128, bool, datetime, timestamp, an embedded document, an array, a regex, null and an object id. The declared word and the value together choose the width (design section 2a), so a driver tests its choice against these bytes.

vectors.name: ring keyed: an insert of a binary and a uuid
vectors.notes: A binary is BSON binary with subtype 0 unless the driver is given one; a uuid is subtype 4. Both are one type byte, so a driver that writes a uuid as a plain binary writes another value.

vectors.name: ring keyed: a document id with a zero byte
vectors.notes: The client sends the id twice: IDValue is the id as a typed BSON value, and the 20-byte prologue's header carries the encID, which is the same value in the store's key encoding. A binary id holds a zero byte, so the encID writes it as 0x00 0xFF and ends the component with 0x00 0x00; a driver reads the id back from IDValue and never from the encoding.

vectors.name: ring keyed: a document id at the 1024-byte cap
vectors.notes: An encID is 1 to 1024 bytes: this one is 510 zero bytes and one more, escaped, which fills the cap exactly. A driver must frame it rather than assume a shorter id.

vectors.name: ring store: nearest by dot product
vectors.notes: Metric 0x02 is the dot product: the score is the sum of the products, higher is closer, and the vector need not be normalized. Scores are doubles, one per element, best first.

vectors.name: ring store: nearest by L2 distance
vectors.notes: Metric 0x03 is the squared L2 distance: the score is the sum of the squared differences, lower is closer, and it is the one metric where the lowest score wins.

vectors.name: ring admin: show buckets
vectors.notes: show_buckets takes database and optionally limit and cursor, and answers one page in database then name order: buckets, each {name, bucket_id, state}, then more and cursor. A page that is not the last writes the last name it sent as the cursor, and the next request sends it back unchanged.

vectors.name: ring admin: show databases
vectors.notes: show_databases takes limit and cursor, never a database, and answers the databases the session may see: databases, each {name, id, rf}, then more and cursor, which is the last name of a page that is not the last.

vectors.name: ring admin: describe a database
vectors.notes: describe_database takes database and optionally limit and cursor, and answers name, database_id, rf and storage, then one page of its buckets as show_buckets lists them. memory_bytes and memory_cap_bytes are written for a memory database only.

vectors.name: ring admin: describe the node that answers
vectors.notes: describe_node takes nothing but cmd and answers the node's own facts: node_id, version, uptime_ms, member_state, members, voters, epoch, leader, default_rf, serving, then the optional state_range and refused_peers, and host, which is absent when the server cannot read the machine. A witness answers serving no_quorum and is never a data node.

vectors.name: ring keyed: a deduped retry answers with the document
vectors.notes: A retry under a request id the dedupe window still holds is answered deduped true with the same reply, including the document a return asked for: nothing was written twice, and a driver must not read deduped as a failure.

vectors.name: ring keyed: a deduped retry whose document was too large to keep
vectors.notes: A recorded document over the dedupe entry's 1024 bytes is not kept, so the retry answers deduped true with document_truncated true and no document: the write was applied once, and the caller reads the document with a get.

vectors.name: ring list: an expand whose where filtered far documents
vectors.notes: expand_filtered is how many far documents a where excluded, written only when an expansion carried a where (a present zero is written then too). expanded still has one entry per row, so a driver pairs them by position and reads the count as what it did not see.

vectors.name: ring keyed: an insert of a document that exists
vectors.notes: DOCUMENT_EXISTS (0x12, exit 2): insert never replaces, and the text names upsert.

payload_json.message: document "ada" is already in app.User, and insert never replaces. Run 'db.User.upsert({_id_: "ada", …})' to replace it, or 'db.User["ada"].get()' to read what is there

vectors.name: ring keyed: a read the owner did not answer
vectors.notes: OWNER_DOWN (0x15, exit 8) carries the detail {owner, missing_slots}: the nodes that own the slots a call must read did not answer, and a partial answer would look complete. The client retries or starts a replacement.

payload_json.message: get app.User: node-b owns 3 of the 8192 slots this call must read and did not answer, so a partial result would look complete. Nothing was returned. Run 'nodes' to see node-b; retry in a few seconds, or start its replacement with 'replace-node node-b --with node-b@<addr>'

vectors.name: ring keyed: a node that cannot see a majority
vectors.notes: NO_QUORUM (0x16, exit 8) carries the detail {voters, answered}: the node refuses reads and writes rather than answer from a copy that may be behind. The client waits for a majority.

payload_json.message: this node cannot see a majority of the cluster's 3 voters (1 answered), so it refuses reads and writes: what it holds may be missing acknowledged writes. Run 'nodes' to see which voters are down, and retry when a majority answers

vectors.name: ring admin: a replication factor the cluster cannot hold
vectors.notes: RF_UNSUPPORTED (0x17, exit 2) carries the detail {rf, voters, data_members}: the database was not created, and the text names the node that must join first.

payload_json.message: replication factor 3 needs at least 3 voters, at least 3 of them holding data; this cluster has 2 voters and 2 data members. Run 'nodes' to see the members, add a data node with 'join <node>@<addr>', or set 'alter database app { replication_factor: 3 }'

vectors.name: ring keyed: a claim on a node whose lease lapsed
vectors.notes: LEASE_LAPSED (0x18, exit 8) carries the detail {node, lapsed_ms, step_down_ms}: the node stopped serving because it could not renew its lease, and the cluster elects another owner.

payload_json.message: node node-b stopped serving reads and writes 4500 ms ago because it could not renew its lease (step_down_ms 3000). Nothing was written. Run 'nodes': the cluster elects an owner for the slot, then retry; 'show placement for <id> in <db>.<bucket>' names it

vectors.name: ring keyed: a frame from an epoch this node has fenced off
vectors.notes: EPOCH_FENCED (0x19, exit 0) is node to node: a frame carries an epoch below the one this node has applied, and the reply says which. No client acts on it, and a driver still maps the code to its own class.

payload_json.message: refused append from node-b at epoch 4: this node is at epoch 3

vectors.name: ring keyed: a position that skips a sequence number
vectors.notes: SEQ_GAP (0x1A, exit 0) is node to node: a copy was offered a position it does not follow, names the one it holds and the range it is missing, and catches up.

payload_json.message: refused position 4:7 for slot 5737 of app from node-b: this copy is at 4:5, and 4:6…4:7 are missing. Catching up; no client action

vectors.name: ring keyed: a log that no longer reaches the copy
vectors.notes: LOG_BELOW_HORIZON (0x1B, exit 8): the record a copy needs is older than the log keeps, so the copy stays behind until the slot is seeded again.

payload_json.message: cannot catch node-b up for slot 5737 of app: it needs 4:900 and the log's oldest record for the slot is 4:1000 (600 s kept, 268435456 cap). The copy stays behind until the slot is re-seeded, which this build does not start by itself; the slot is served by its other copies

vectors.name: ring admin: a command built on a state the cluster has left
vectors.notes: STATE_MOVED (0x1C, exit 8): the command was built on a state sequence the cluster has moved past, nothing was changed, and the same command is built again from the new state.

payload_json.message: refused: the cluster state moved to state_seq 10 while this command was built on 9. Nothing was changed. Re-run it ('nodes' prints the current state_seq)

vectors.name: ring admin: a replacement of a node that is still up
vectors.notes: CONFLICT (0x1D, exit 8): a replacement cannot take the identity of a member that is still writing, because both would own its slots.

payload_json.message: node "node-b" is still active at epoch 4, so a replacement cannot take its identity: two nodes writing as node-b would both own its slots. Stop it and wait for it to be declared down ('nodes' shows the state), then 'replace-node node-b --with node-b@<addr>'

vectors.name: ring admin: a node of another cluster
vectors.notes: CLUSTER_MISMATCH (0x1E, exit 2): the joining node holds state of a different cluster, and the text names the join that discards it.

payload_json.message: node "node-d" belongs to cluster a1b2c3d4… but this node belongs to cluster 9f8e7d6c…. Start it with 'join node-d@node-a.example:4433'; its own state is discarded and its documents are re-seeded

vectors.name: ring keyed: a write sent to a witness
vectors.notes: NOT_A_DATA_NODE (0x1F, exit 2): a witness holds the state and a vote and no documents, so a document write sent to it is refused and the text names a data node.

payload_json.message: node "node-w" is a witness: it holds the cluster state and a vote, and no documents. Send this to a data node ('nodes' marks each node data or witness)

vectors.name: ring keyed: a read of a bucket being dropped
vectors.notes: BUCKET_DROPPING (0x21, exit 8): a dropping bucket accepts no reads or writes, the detail-free text names the sweep that has to finish, and the name is free when it does.

payload_json.message: bucket "User" in database "app" is being dropped (4096 of 8192 slots swept), and a dropping bucket accepts no reads or writes. Run 'show buckets in app' to watch it leave the list; the name is free when the sweep finishes and the declaration is deleted

vectors.name: ring keyed: a declaration that cannot be read
vectors.notes: DECL_UNAVAILABLE (0x22, exit 8): the node that holds the declaration did not answer and this node holds no cached copy, so nothing can be checked and nothing was written.

payload_json.message: cannot read the declaration of bucket "User" in database "app": the node that stores it did not answer in time (it may be busy, or down), and this node holds no cached declaration for that name. Nothing was written. Run 'nodes': if every member is active, run 'status' on each node: Serving: ok means the read was only slow, so send the write again; a member that is not active is the one to bring back

vectors.name: ring admin: a bucket that already exists
vectors.notes: BUCKET_EXISTS (0x23, exit 2): create_bucket never re-declares, and the text names the id and the state the name already holds.

payload_json.message: bucket "User" already exists in database "app" with id 1f4a2c9b7de30015, state active. Run 'show buckets in app' to see it, or 'describe bucket User in app' to see its fields and the version it was created with; if the field table differs, this retry is old — re-read the declaration before trying again

vectors.name: ring admin: a bucket name a system bucket holds
vectors.notes: RESERVED_NAME (0x24, exit 2): a name beginning with an underscore belongs to the system, so the create names the rule and a name that works.

payload_json.message: "_buckets" cannot be a bucket name: names beginning with "_" are reserved for system buckets, and every database has the system bucket _buckets, which holds the declaration of each bucket. Run 'show buckets in app' to list the buckets you can create, or choose a name without a leading underscore

vectors.name: ring admin: a bucket id that could not be claimed
vectors.notes: BUCKET_ID_COLLISION (0x25, exit 8): every draw of a free bucket id collided, nothing was created, and the text says a retry draws fresh ids.

payload_json.message: could not claim a free bucket id for "User" in database "app" after 3 draws; nothing was created. Retry 'create bucket User in app { … }': every attempt draws fresh ids

vectors.name: ring admin: a replacement of a node that still holds its documents
vectors.notes: REPLACE_TARGET_HAS_DATA (0x27, exit 8): the new identity's directory holds documents of its own, so the replacement without --clear would claim copies it never seeded.

payload_json.message: node "node-b" cannot be replaced without --clear: its data directory holds 1048576 bytes of documents for this identity, and a replacement that starts with documents of its own would claim copies it never seeded. Run 'replace-node node-b --with node-b@<addr> --clear' to discard them and seed this identity's slots from their current owners

vectors.name: ring keyed: an insert whose id could not be minted
vectors.notes: MINT_FAILED (0x28, exit 8): the insert carried no id and the owner could not mint one, nothing was written, and the text names the id the caller can supply.

payload_json.message: insert could not mint an _id_: the random source did not answer. Nothing was written. Retry, or supply one: 'db.<bucket>.insert({_id_: "<id>", <field>: <value>})'

vectors.name: ring keyed: a stored key that does not decode
vectors.notes: CORRUPT_KEY (0x29, exit 2): the store holds a key whose id component does not decode, so the node refuses rather than guess, and the text is the one that tells the operator to keep the data directory.

payload_json.message: the store holds a key in bucket id 1f4a2c9b7de30015 whose id component does not decode: unknown tag 0x7F at offset 3. Stop this node, move /var/lib/hoarddb/store aside and keep it (its files may be the only copy), then restart and let the node be seeded
